name: Cuba
genZNote: Cuba has run a Communist one-party state literally 90 miles off the coast of Florida since 1959 — a small island nation that became the single most defining Cold War flashpoint in the Western Hemisphere, from the Bay of Pigs to the Missile Crisis.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The largest island in the Caribbean, located just south of Florida, USA, with a long, narrow shape and extensive coastline.
Predominantly flat to gently rolling terrain with fertile plains historically dedicated to sugarcane and tobacco cultivation, and mountain ranges in the southeast.
Tropical climate, prone to Atlantic hurricanes, given its location within the Caribbean hurricane belt.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Spanish is the official language; the culture reflects a rich blend of Spanish colonial, African (brought via the slave trade), and indigenous Taíno influences.
World-renowned for its music (son, salsa, mambo) and dance traditions, alongside a strong literary and artistic heritage.
Baseball is the most popular national sport, a cultural legacy connected to Cuba's historical ties with the United States before the 1959 revolution.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A single-party socialist republic governed by the Communist Party of Cuba since the 1959 revolution led by Fidel Castro, which overthrew the Batista government.
Cuba operates a centrally planned economy alongside gradually expanding private enterprise reforms introduced in recent years.
Subject to a long-standing US trade embargo since the early 1960s, a central and enduring feature of its international economic relations.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Globally renowned for its healthcare system and medical training, exporting large numbers of doctors on international humanitarian missions to other developing countries.
Achieved notably strong public health outcomes (life expectancy, doctor-to-population ratio) despite its modest income level, a widely studied development case.
Developed its own domestically produced COVID-19 vaccines (e.g., Abdala, Soberana), a notable achievement for a small, sanctioned economy.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Has faced a comprehensive US trade embargo since the early 1960s, significantly shaping its economic development and international alliances.
Historically closely allied with the Soviet Union during the Cold War, and more recently with Venezuela, China, and Russia.
Played a central role in several major Cold War flashpoints, including the 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion and the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Cuba have maintained friendly relations since 1959, rooted in shared participation in the Non-Aligned Movement.
India has periodically extended humanitarian and medical assistance to Cuba, and the two countries collaborate on pharmaceutical and biotechnology research exchange.
Trade remains modest, constrained partly by the long-standing US embargo's effect on Cuba's broader international economic engagement.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A centrally planned economy historically dependent on sugar exports, now increasingly reliant on tourism, remittances, and medical service exports.
The long-standing US trade embargo has significantly constrained Cuba's access to international trade, finance, and technology.
Gradual market-oriented reforms in recent years have expanded small-scale private enterprise ('cuentapropismo').

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The 1959 Cuban Revolution led by Fidel Castro and Che Guevara.
A globally admired public healthcare and medical training system despite economic sanctions.
Vibrant music traditions including son, salsa, and mambo.
The 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, a defining Cold War confrontation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Cuba is a single-party socialist republic in the Caribbean, governed by the Communist Party since the 1959 revolution, known for its healthcare system and long-standing US trade embargo.
keyFacts: Single-party socialist republic under the Communist Party since the 1959 revolution.
Subject to a comprehensive US trade embargo since the early 1960s.
Globally recognised for its healthcare system and medical missions abroad.
commonConfusion: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) and the Bay of Pigs invasion (1961) are two separate Cold War events — the invasion came first and failed, the missile crisis followed a year later.

highYieldFacts: Cuba: single-party socialist republic since the 1959 revolution; capital Havana.
Long-standing US trade embargo since the early 1960s; central Cold War flashpoint (Bay of Pigs 1961, Missile Crisis 1962).
India-Cuba: friendly ties since 1959 via the Non-Aligned Movement; periodic medical/humanitarian cooperation.
commonTraps: Confusing the 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion with the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis — distinct events a year apart.
Assuming Cuba's economy is purely state-run today — gradual private enterprise reforms have been introduced in recent years.
mustRemember: Cuba: socialist republic since 1959, US-embargoed, healthcare/medical-mission leader, longstanding Non-Aligned Movement partner with India.
